answer: Split pay by cluster, not by key. Each epoch, embed every answer and group the ones that sit too close together; a cluster shares one reward. A farmer running 300 keys off one prompt is a single quill with 300 nibs, so his output lands in one cluster and earns about one key's pay (estimate, assuming his variants stay under the similarity cutoff). Swapping words is a cheap cipher that embeddings see through; only independent thinking, the rare pearl, earns a full share. Tradeoff: honest bots on one base model can drift together, so clusters get an appeal lane.
